recipe.name: Sabudana Thalipeeth
steps: Rinse the sabudana in a sieve until the runoff is almost clear. Place in a bowl with the measured water, cover and soak for 4–6 hours, until a pearl crushes easily between your fingers without a hard centre. Drain any unabsorbed water thoroughly.

While the pearls soak, simmer the whole potatoes in a separate pan of water for 20–25 minutes, until a knife slides through. Drain, cool enough to handle, peel and mash smoothly; discard the cooking water.

Crush the roasted peanuts coarsely. Finely chop the chilli and coriander, then mix with the drained pearls, potato, cumin, lemon juice and rock salt. Squeeze a small portion: it should hold together without dripping moisture.

Divide into eight portions. With damp fingers, pat each portion on a small piece of baking parchment into a disc about 12 cm wide and 5 mm thick. Make a small hole in the centre so the middle cooks evenly.
Heat a heavy griddle over medium heat. Brush with a little of the measured oil, invert a disc onto it and peel away the parchment immediately. Spoon a little oil around the edge and into the centre.

Cook for 4–5 minutes until the underside has golden patches and releases easily. Turn carefully and cook the other side for 3–4 minutes; the pearls should look translucent and the centre should be set, with no raw crunch. Repeat with the remaining discs and oil.
tips: Very wet pearls make the dough sticky; drain well before mixing. Serve two small thalipeeth per person.
recipe.passiveTime: Soak sabudana for 4–6 hours; allow potatoes to cool for about 15 minutes.

recipe.name: Farali Pattice
steps: Simmer the whole potatoes in water for 25–30 minutes until tender through the centre. Drain completely, peel while warm and mash without adding water. Spread on a plate to cool for 20 minutes so steam escapes.

Grate the coconut and ginger, chop the cashews and raisins, and crush the roasted peanuts. Mix these with finely chopped chilli and coriander, lemon juice, sugar and half the rock salt to make a moist, loose filling.
Mix the cooled potato with 40 g of the arrowroot flour and the remaining salt. Divide into eight portions. Keep the remaining 20 g flour on a plate for dusting.

Flatten a potato portion in your palm, add one eighth of the filling, and bring the edges together. Seal completely, then flatten gently into a thick patty. Repeat, keeping the filling enclosed so it cannot spill into the oil.

Dust each patty lightly with the reserved arrowroot. Heat half the oil in a heavy frying pan over medium heat and add four patties without crowding. Shallow-fry for 4–5 minutes without moving them until a firm golden crust forms.

Turn with a broad spatula and cook for another 4–5 minutes until both faces are crisp and the centre is hot. Drain briefly on kitchen paper. Cook the second batch with the remaining oil and serve two patties per person.
tips: This is a shallow-fried potato-shell version with coconut and dry-fruit filling; the oil quantity is for the pan, not a measured absorbed amount.
recipe.passiveTime: Cool the mashed potatoes for 20 minutes before shaping.

gu.Four adult portions. Listed time covers: ચાર પુખ્ત વ્યક્તિઓ માટે. આપેલો સમય તૈયારી અને રાંધવાનો છે; વધારાનો પલાળવાનો, ઠંડું કરવાનો કે રાખવાનો સમય અલગ છે. ઉપવાસની પ્રથાઓ જુદી હોય છે: દરેક સામગ્રી પરિવારની પ્રથા પ્રમાણે તપાસો. જૈન યોગ્યતા તમારી સાચવેલી સામગ્રીની પસંદ પર આધારિત છે.

recipe.name: Samak Pulao
steps: Pick over the barnyard millet, rinse in a fine sieve and soak in fresh water for 15 minutes. Drain completely; this soaking water is separate from the measured cooking water.
Peel the potato and cut into 1 cm cubes. Finely chop the chilli and coriander. Measure the cooking water before starting so the small grains do not sit in the hot pan too long.
Warm the ghee in a heavy saucepan. Fry the peanuts over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes until lightly golden, then lift them out. Add cumin to the remaining ghee and let it sizzle.
Add potato and chilli and cook for 3 minutes, turning often. Stir in the drained millet for 30 seconds, then add the measured water and rock salt. Bring to a gentle boil.

Cover and cook over low heat for 12–15 minutes until the water is absorbed, the potato is tender and the millet is soft. If the grains remain firm, add a small splash of hot water and cook covered for 2 minutes more.
Remove from the heat and rest covered for 5 minutes. Fold in the fried peanuts, lemon juice and coriander gently with a fork; avoid vigorous stirring, which makes the millet pasty.
tips: Samak is barnyard millet, not ordinary rice. This potato-and-peanut version is not automatically suitable for a Jain household.
recipe.passiveTime: Soak millet for 15 minutes; rest the cooked pulao for 5 minutes.

hi.Pick over the barnyard millet, rinse in: सामक चुनकर बारीक छलनी में धोएँ और साफ पानी में 15 मिनट भिगोएँ। पूरा पानी छान दें। भिगोने का पानी नापे हुए पकाने के पानी से अलग है।
आलू छीलकर 1 सेमी के टुकड़े करें। मिर्च और धनिया बारीक काटें। पकाने का पानी पहले नाप लें ताकि छोटे दाने गरम पैन में ज्यादा देर न रहें।
hi.Warm the ghee in a heavy saucepan. Fry t: भारी पतीले में घी गरम करें। मूँगफली मध्यम-धीमी आँच पर 3–4 मिनट हल्की सुनहरी होने तक तलकर निकालें। बचे घी में जीरा डालकर चटकने दें।
hi.Add potato and chilli and cook for 3 min: आलू और मिर्च डालकर 3 मिनट चलाते हुए पकाएँ। छना सामक डालकर 30 सेकंड चलाएँ। नापा पानी और सेंधा नमक डालकर हल्का उबाल लें।
hi.Cover and cook over low heat for 12–15 m: ढककर धीमी आँच पर 12–15 मिनट पकाएँ, जब तक पानी सूख जाए, आलू नरम हो और सामक पक जाए। दाने सख्त हों तो थोड़ा गरम पानी डालकर ढकें और 2 मिनट और पकाएँ।
hi.Remove from the heat and rest covered fo: आँच बंद करके ढका हुआ 5 मिनट रखें। मूँगफली, नींबू का रस और धनिया काँटे से हल्के हाथ मिलाएँ। जोर से चलाने पर सामक चिपचिपा हो सकता है।
hi.Samak is barnyard millet, not ordinary r: सामक एक प्रकार का छोटा अनाज है, सामान्य चावल नहीं। आलू और मूँगफली वाला यह रूप अपने आप जैन परिवार के लिए उपयुक्त नहीं माना जाता।
hi.Soak millet for 15 minutes; rest the coo: सामक 15 मिनट भिगोएँ; पके पुलाव को 5 मिनट ढककर रखें।
hi.Four adult portions. Listed time covers: चार वयस्कों के लिए। दिया समय तैयारी और पकाने का है; अतिरिक्त भिगोने, ठंडा करने या रखने का समय अलग है। व्रत की परंपराएँ अलग होती हैं: हर सामग्री अपने परिवार की प्रथा से जाँचें। जैन उपयुक्तता आपकी सहेजी सामग्री-पसंद पर निर्भर है।

gu.Pick over the barnyard millet, rinse in: સામો વીણી બારીક ચાળણીમાં ધુઓ અને સ્વચ્છ પાણીમાં 15 મિનિટ પલાળો. પાણી સંપૂર્ણ નિતારો. પલાળવાનું પાણી માપેલા રાંધવાના પાણીથી અલગ છે.
બટાકાની છાલ ઉતારી 1 સેમીના ટુકડા કરો. મરચું અને કોથમીર ઝીણાં કાપો. રાંધવાનું પાણી પહેલાં માપી રાખો જેથી નાના દાણા ગરમ પેનમાં વધારે વાર ન રહે.
gu.Warm the ghee in a heavy saucepan. Fry t: ભારે તપેલીમાં ઘી ગરમ કરો. મગફળી મધ્યમ-ધીમા તાપે 3–4 મિનિટ હળવી સોનેરી થાય ત્યાં સુધી તળી કાઢો. બાકી ઘીમાં જીરું નાખીને તતડવા દો.
gu.Add potato and chilli and cook for 3 min: બટાકા અને મરચું નાખી 3 મિનિટ વારંવાર ફેરવતાં પકાવો. નિતારેલો સામો 30 સેકન્ડ હલાવો, પછી માપેલું પાણી અને સિંધવ મીઠું ઉમેરી હળવો ઊભરો આવવા દો.
gu.Cover and cook over low heat for 12–15 m: ઢાંકીને ધીમા તાપે 12–15 મિનિટ પકાવો, પાણી શોષાય, બટાકા નરમ થાય અને સામો ચડે ત્યાં સુધી. દાણા કઠણ હોય તો થોડું ગરમ પાણી નાખી ઢાંકીને 2 મિનિટ વધુ પકાવો.
gu.Remove from the heat and rest covered fo: તાપ બંધ કરીને ઢાંકેલું 5 મિનિટ રહેવા દો. તળેલી મગફળી, લીંબુનો રસ અને કોથમીર કાંટાથી હળવેથી ભેળવો. જોરથી હલાવવાથી સામો ચીકણો થાય છે.
gu.Samak is barnyard millet, not ordinary r: સામો નાનું ધાન્ય છે, સામાન્ય ચોખા નથી. બટાકા અને મગફળીવાળું આ સ્વરૂપ આપમેળે જૈન પરિવાર માટે યોગ્ય ગણાતું નથી.
gu.Soak millet for 15 minutes; rest the coo: સામો 15 મિનિટ પલાળો; ચડેલો પુલાવ 5 મિનિટ ઢાંકીને રાખો.
gu.Four adult portions. Listed time covers: ચાર પુખ્ત વ્યક્તિઓ માટે. આપેલો સમય તૈયારી અને રાંધવાનો છે; વધારાનો પલાળવાનો, ઠંડું કરવાનો કે રાખવાનો સમય અલગ છે. ઉપવાસની પ્રથાઓ જુદી હોય છે: દરેક સામગ્રી પરિવારની પ્રથા પ્રમાણે તપાસો. જૈન યોગ્યતા તમારી સાચવેલી સામગ્રીની પસંદ પર આધારિત છે.

recipe.name: Kuttu Paratha
steps: Boil the whole potatoes in a separate pan of water for 20–25 minutes until tender. Drain well, peel and mash while warm. Let the mash cool for 15 minutes; it must not be wet or steaming when mixed with flour.
Reserve 20 g buckwheat flour for dusting. Mix the remaining flour with the potato, crushed cumin, finely chopped chilli and coriander, and rock salt.
Add the measured water a spoonful at a time, using only enough to bring the mixture into a soft dough. Knead gently just until smooth; buckwheat dough does not stretch like wheat dough.
Divide into eight portions. Dust parchment with some reserved flour and pat or gently roll each portion into a disc about 13 cm across and 3–4 mm thick. Repair cracks at the edges with damp fingers.
Transfer a disc to a medium-hot griddle and cook for about 1 minute until the top loses its wet appearance. Turn, spread a little ghee over the surface and cook for 2 minutes.

Turn again and cook with a little more ghee until both sides have brown patches and the centre is cooked, pressing the edges lightly with a spatula. Use the remaining ghee for the other parathas and serve hot.
tips: Potato binds the naturally gluten-free flour. Do not replace it silently when assessing household restrictions.
recipe.passiveTime: Cool the potato mash for 15 minutes.

hi.Boil the whole potatoes in a separate pa: साबुत आलू अलग पानी में 20–25 मिनट नरम होने तक उबालें। पानी निकालकर गरम रहते छीलें और मसलें। 15 मिनट ठंडा करें; आटे में मिलाते समय आलू गीले या भाप छोड़ते हुए नहीं होने चाहिए।
hi.Reserve 20 g buckwheat flour for dusting: बेलने के लिए 20 ग्राम कुट्टू का आटा अलग रखें। बाकी आटे में आलू, कुटा जीरा, बारीक मिर्च, धनिया और सेंधा नमक मिलाएँ।
hi.Add the measured water a spoonful at a t: नापा पानी चम्मच-चम्मच डालें, केवल उतना जितने में नरम आटा बँध जाए। हल्के हाथ चिकना करें; कुट्टू का आटा गेहूँ के आटे की तरह खिंचता नहीं है।
hi.Divide into eight portions. Dust parchme: आठ भाग करें। कागज पर अलग रखा आटा छिड़कें और हर भाग को थपथपाकर या हल्के हाथ बेलकर लगभग 13 सेमी चौड़ा, 3–4 मिमी मोटा बनाएँ। किनारों की दरारें गीली उँगलियों से जोड़ें।
hi.Transfer a disc to a medium-hot griddle: मध्यम गरम तवे पर पराठा रखें और लगभग 1 मिनट पकाएँ, जब तक ऊपर का गीलापन खत्म हो। पलटें, थोड़ा घी लगाएँ और 2 मिनट पकाएँ।
hi.Turn again and cook with a little more g: फिर पलटकर थोड़ा घी लगाएँ और दोनों ओर भूरे धब्बे आने तथा बीच तक पकने तक पकाएँ। किनारे हल्के दबाएँ। बाकी पराठे बचे घी में बनाकर गरम परोसें।
hi.Potato binds the naturally gluten-free f: आलू स्वाभाविक रूप से ग्लूटेन-रहित आटे को बाँधता है। परिवार के प्रतिबंध जाँचते समय इसे बिना बताए न बदलें।
hi.Four adult portions. Listed time covers: चार वयस्कों के लिए। दिया समय तैयारी और पकाने का है; अतिरिक्त भिगोने, ठंडा करने या रखने का समय अलग है। व्रत की परंपराएँ अलग होती हैं: हर सामग्री अपने परिवार की प्रथा से जाँचें। जैन उपयुक्तता आपकी सहेजी सामग्री-पसंद पर निर्भर है।

gu.Boil the whole potatoes in a separate pa: આખા બટાકા અલગ પાણીમાં 20–25 મિનિટ નરમ થાય ત્યાં સુધી ઉકાળો. પાણી નિતારી ગરમ હોય ત્યારે છોલીને મસળો. 15 મિનિટ ઠંડા કરો; લોટમાં ભેળવતી વખતે ભીના કે વરાળવાળા ન હોવા જોઈએ.
gu.Reserve 20 g buckwheat flour for dusting: વણવા માટે 20 ગ્રામ કુટ્ટુનો લોટ અલગ રાખો. બાકીના લોટમાં બટાકા, કૂટેલું જીરું, ઝીણું મરચું, કોથમીર અને સિંધવ મીઠું ભેળવો.
gu.Add the measured water a spoonful at a t: માપેલું પાણી ચમચી-ચમચી ઉમેરો, નરમ લોટ બંધાય એટલું જ લો. હળવેથી સુંવાળો કરો; કુટ્ટુનો લોટ ઘઉંની જેમ ખેંચાતો નથી.
gu.Divide into eight portions. Dust parchme: આઠ ભાગ કરો. કાગળ પર રાખેલો લોટ ભભરાવી દરેક ભાગ હળવેથી વણો કે થાપો: આશરે 13 સેમી પહોળો અને 3–4 મિમી જાડો. કિનારીની તિરાડો ભીની આંગળીથી જોડો.
gu.Transfer a disc to a medium-hot griddle: મધ્યમ ગરમ તવા પર મૂકી આશરે 1 મિનિટ શેકો, ઉપરની ભીનાશ જાય ત્યાં સુધી. ફેરવો, થોડું ઘી લગાવી 2 મિનિટ શેકો.
gu.Turn again and cook with a little more g: ફરી ફેરવી થોડું ઘી લગાવો અને બંને બાજુ ભૂરા ડાઘ પડે તથા વચ્ચે સુધી ચડે ત્યાં સુધી શેકો. કિનારીઓ હળવી દબાવો. બાકીના પરાઠા બાકી ઘીથી બનાવી ગરમ પીરસો.
gu.Potato binds the naturally gluten-free f: બટાકો કુદરતી રીતે ગ્લુટેન વગરના લોટને બાંધે છે. પરિવારના પ્રતિબંધ તપાસતી વખતે જાણ કર્યા વગર તેને બદલો નહીં.
gu.Four adult portions. Listed time covers: ચાર પુખ્ત વ્યક્તિઓ માટે. આપેલો સમય તૈયારી અને રાંધવાનો છે; વધારાનો પલાળવાનો, ઠંડું કરવાનો કે રાખવાનો સમય અલગ છે. ઉપવાસની પ્રથાઓ જુદી હોય છે: દરેક સામગ્રી પરિવારની પ્રથા પ્રમાણે તપાસો. જૈન યોગ્યતા તમારી સાચવેલી સામગ્રીની પસંદ પર આધારિત છે.

recipe.name: Kuttu Pakora
steps: Peel the potatoes and slice into even 2 mm rounds; thicker slices can stay raw after the batter browns. Pat the slices dry. Finely chop the chilli and coriander.
Mix buckwheat flour, cumin, chilli, coriander and rock salt. Whisk in the water gradually to make a smooth batter that coats a spoon thickly but still falls in a ribbon.
Pour the oil into a deep, heavy pan with plenty of headroom and heat to about 170°C. A small drop of batter should rise steadily with bubbles, not sink or darken immediately.
Dip a potato slice into the batter, let the excess drip briefly and lower it carefully into the oil. Add a few more without crowding or letting the slices stick together.

Fry for 4–6 minutes, turning halfway, until the coating is crisp and the bubbles have slowed. Cut open the first pakora: the potato must be completely tender, with no firm raw centre. Reduce the heat slightly if the outside colours too quickly.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain. Bring the oil back to temperature before frying the next batch. Keep water away from the hot oil and serve the pakoras freshly cooked.
tips: The 600 ml oil is the frying medium, not the amount absorbed. Never fill the pan more than halfway with oil.

recipe.name: Singhare ki Puri
steps: Boil the whole potatoes in a separate pan of water for about 20–25 minutes, until a knife reaches the centre easily. Drain, peel and mash smoothly. Cool for 15 minutes so excess steam escapes.

Reserve 20 g of the flour for dusting. Mix the remaining water chestnut flour with potato, crushed cumin, rock salt and 10 ml oil. Add the measured water gradually, stopping as soon as a smooth, firm dough forms.

Divide the dough into twelve equal portions. Dust lightly with the reserved flour and roll gently between parchment into discs about 9 cm wide and 3 mm thick. Keep the thickness even and repair cracked edges.
Heat the remaining 600 ml oil in a deep pan to about 175°C, keeping the pan less than half full. Test a tiny piece of dough: it should rise promptly without becoming dark at once.

Slide in one puri carefully. Gently nudge the surface with a slotted spoon as it rises; turn after about 30–45 seconds. Cook the second side until both faces are lightly golden and no wet dough remains at the rim.

Drain on kitchen paper and repeat, letting the oil regain heat between puris. Open the first puri to check the middle is cooked; lower the heat slightly and cook longer if it browns before cooking through.
tips: Makes twelve small puris, three per person as an accompaniment. Potato binds this traditional dough; check it against your household restrictions.

recipe.name: Singhare ke Pakode
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut into matchsticks no thicker than 3 mm so they cook at the same rate as the batter. Pat dry, and finely chop the chilli and coriander.
Mix water chestnut flour, cumin, rock salt, chilli and coriander. Add the measured water gradually to make a thick batter, then fold in the potato. The mixture should hold a small mound on a spoon.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pan to about 170°C with the pan less than half full. Test a little batter: it should rise with steady bubbles, without immediately turning dark.
Lower small spoonfuls into the oil, keeping each mound about 3 cm across. Leave room between them and do not flatten them against the bottom of the pan.

Fry for 5–6 minutes, turning several times, until crisp and golden. Split the first pakora to check that the potato is tender and the centre has no wet flour; make later portions smaller if the centre cooks too slowly.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain well. Let the oil return to temperature between batches. Serve promptly, since steam softens the crust as the pakode stand.
tips: This potato version contains roots. The measured oil is the quantity needed in the frying pan, not the absorbed amount.

recipe.name: Sweet Potato Chaat
steps: Scrub the sweet potatoes and rinse off all soil. Place them whole in a heavy covered pan over low heat, without oil, using similarly sized roots so they roast evenly.

Cook for 35–45 minutes, turning every 6–8 minutes with tongs. The skins may blister; lower the heat if they scorch quickly. Test the thickest part with a skewer: it should pass through without resistance.
While the sweet potatoes cook, toast the cumin in a small dry pan for about 1 minute until fragrant. Cool briefly and crush with the black pepper. Finely chop the coriander.
Rest the cooked sweet potatoes off the heat for 5 minutes. Peel carefully while warm and remove any charred skin; cut the soft flesh into bite-sized chunks.
Place the chunks in a bowl and sprinkle with the crushed spices and rock salt. Add lemon juice and turn gently so the pieces are seasoned without being mashed.
Finish with coriander and serve warm. Taste a piece before serving; the lemon should balance the natural sweetness without pooling at the bottom.

recipe.name: Vrat Wale Aloo
steps: Wash the potatoes and simmer whole in a pan of water for 20–25 minutes until just tender. Test with a knife; the centres should be cooked but the potatoes should not fall apart. Drain fully.
Let the potatoes cool for 10 minutes, then peel and cut into 2 cm chunks. Chop the chilli and coriander, and crush the black pepper.
Heat ghee in a broad heavy pan over medium heat. Add cumin and let it sizzle for 20–30 seconds until aromatic, then add the chilli and stir briefly.
Add the potatoes in a fairly even layer. Cook for 4–5 minutes without frequent stirring so the undersides develop golden patches, then turn carefully.
Sprinkle with rock salt and black pepper. Cook for another 3–4 minutes, turning once or twice, until the edges are lightly crisp and the centres are hot.
Switch off the heat and fold in lemon juice and coriander. Serve as a potato accompaniment with your chosen fasting bread; it is not a complete meal by itself.
tips: Keep the potato pieces intact rather than mashing them into the cumin tempering.

recipe.name: Shengdana Amti
steps: Rub the roasted peanuts to loosen the skins and discard any loose skins. Grind the nuts with grated fresh coconut, chopped chilli and 200 ml of the measured water to a smooth paste.
Heat ghee in a heavy saucepan over medium-low heat. Add cumin and let it sizzle until fragrant, keeping it pale brown rather than black.
Lower the heat and carefully stir in the peanut paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring the bottom constantly because nut paste catches easily.
Add the remaining 600 ml water gradually, whisking out lumps. Add jaggery and rock salt and bring to a gentle simmer rather than a rapid boil.
Simmer uncovered for 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until the raw paste aroma has gone and the curry lightly coats a spoon. Add a little hot water if it becomes too thick; amti should be pourable.
Take off the heat and stir in the lemon juice. Taste for a gentle sweet-sour balance and serve hot alongside your chosen bhagar or fasting bread, prepared separately.
